observation.visible_scene: A broad natural waterfall seen from a cliff-top vantage: a wide, turbulent sheet of white water pours over a rock lip into a deep gorge, with a calm grey river approaching the brink at the upper left, dense green trees and shrubs crowning the cliff edge and a band of leafy vegetation across the bottom foreground. On the right a separate, taller vertical fall drops into a canyon filled with rising white mist.
visible_changes: The main white-water sheet churns continuously: foam crests and streaks deform and translate downward over the lip throughout the excerpt, with no start or stop visible.
The dark river surface above the brink shows steady forward motion toward the edge (white streaks advancing).
The vertical fall on the right and the mist column below it billow and shift shape frame to frame, indicating ongoing flow and rising spray.

The framing drifts gradually across the clip: the tree mass at the far-left corner present in the first frames moves out of view, the left river opening widens, and the right-hand vertical fall shifts leftward within the frame, consistent with a slow camera pan/zoom rather than any object moving.
Foreground shrubs at the bottom remain in place relative to the camera but their position relative to the cliff edge changes with the framing drift.
outside_clip_unknowns: The bottom of the gorge and where the falling water lands are not visible.
Whether the flow rate or weather changed before or after this segment is unknown.
The cause of the camera drift (handheld move vs. zoom) is not determinable from the frames alone.
uncertain_details: Exact camera motion type (pan right vs. slight zoom-out) is uncertain; only the relative shift of static background features is clear.
Mist movement cannot be cleanly separated between wind drift and turbulence from the falls.
The water sheet's overall extent is constant; apparent changes are texture deformation, not the sheet growing or shrinking.
